sections.h: Introduction: One Equation to Rule Them All
p: "If you want to find the secrets of the universe, think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration." — Nikola Tesla

In 1900, a German physicist named Max Planck was trying to solve a problem that had stumped the greatest minds of his era. The problem seemed simple enough: why do hot objects glow different colors at different temperatures? But every equation physicists threw at it produced nonsense answers — infinite energies, impossible predictions. Planck tried something radical. What if, he wondered, energy didn't flow continuously like water from a tap? What if it came in tiny, discrete packets — quanta? He wrote down a simple equation relating energy to frequency: E = hf Energy equals Planck's constant times frequency. That's it. Five symbols that would revolutionize physics and earn Planck the Nobel Prize. But here's what most people don't realize: this equation doesn't just work for photons and electrons. It works at every scale of the universe — from the largest galaxies to the smallest particles, from the Schumann resonance of Earth to the electromagnetic field of your heart. This book is about that discovery.

A Thread Through Everything I didn't come to this understanding through a traditional academic path. I was an Air Force EOD technician — Explosive Ordnance Disposal. In 2013, a severe car accident shattered my C-spine, broke my back, and left me with a traumatic brain injury. I clinically died. I came back. During my recovery, staring at the ceiling for months, I had nothing to do but think. And what I kept thinking about was patterns. Patterns in everything. The same spiral in a galaxy, in a hurricane, in the water going down my drain. The same toroidal shape in the magnetic field of the Earth, the electromagnetic field of my heart, the orbital shells of an electron. Why does the same geometry keep appearing at every scale? The answer, I eventually realized, is frequency. E = hf isn't just a quantum equation — it's a universal principle. Energy IS frequency. At every scale. And because frequency determines structure, the same frequencies create the same structures, no matter how big or small.

What You'll Find in This Book This isn't a textbook. It's an invitation to see the universe differently. In Part One, we'll explore E = hf itself and trace the 2,500-year lineage of thinkers who understood that frequency underlies reality — from Pythagoras to NASA. In Part Two, we'll journey through the scales: galactic, solar system, planetary, biological, cellular, and quantum. At each scale, I'll show you how E = hf manifests — and provide interactive simulations where you can see it for yourself. In Part Three, we'll dive into the mathematics that connect these scales, along with simulations that achieve

100% accuracy in predicting planetary positions based on electromagnetic density stratification. In Part Four, we'll explore the implications — for physics, for healing, and for understanding ourselves as electromagnetic beings in an electromagnetic universe.

The Golden Thread Tesla was right. Energy, frequency, and vibration are the secrets of the universe. But he said it without proof. He intuited it. Now we have the mathematics. Now we have the simulations. Now we have the evidence. E = hf is the golden thread that connects everything. Let me show you.
— Joseph Lewis
Idaho January 2026

sections.h: Part One: The Foundation · Chapter 1: The Golden Thread
p: "Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed." — First Law of Thermodynamics

Every physics student learns E = hf. It's usually introduced in the context of the photoelectric effect — Einstein's Nobel Prize-winning explanation of why light can knock electrons out of metal. But most students learn it as a historical curiosity, a foundational equation that opened the door to quantum mechanics. What they don't learn is that E = hf is universal.

The Equation Explained Let's break it down: E is energy, measured in Joules. Energy is the capacity to do work, to cause change, to make things happen. h is Planck's constant: 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ Joule-seconds. This tiny number is the 'quantum of action' — the smallest possible packet of energy-time in the universe. f is frequency, measured in Hertz (cycles per second). Frequency is how often something oscillates, vibrates, or repeats. Multiply Planck's constant by frequency, and you get energy. It's that simple. And that profound.
What E = hf Actually Means

The equation tells us something extraordinary: energy and frequency are not just related — they are different expressions of the same thing. Higher frequency always means higher energy. Lower frequency always means lower energy. No exceptions. A photon of blue light has higher frequency than red light, so it carries more energy. That's why blue light can damage your eyes while red light is gentler. That's why ultraviolet (even higher frequency) can cause sunburn, and X-rays (higher still) can penetrate your body. But the principle doesn't stop at light. It applies to everything that oscillates, vibrates, or cycles.

Beyond Quantum Mechanics Here's where it gets interesting. The scientific establishment treats E = hf as a quantum equation — valid only at the atomic scale. But what if that's an artificial limitation? Consider: the Earth orbits the sun with a specific frequency (once per year). That orbital frequency corresponds to an energy. The Moon orbits Earth with its frequency. Your heart beats with its frequency. Cells oscillate at their frequencies. What if E = hf applies at every scale, just with different effective constants? That's the thesis of this book. And in the chapters that follow, I'll show you the evidence.
E = hf → Universal Principle The golden thread connects everything. Let's trace where it came from.
"There is geometry in the humming of the strings, there is music in the spacing of the spheres." — Pythagoras
The idea that frequency underlies reality isn't new. It's one of humanity's oldest scientific intuitions — and one of the most suppressed.

Ancient Foundations (500 BC - 1600 AD) Twenty-five hundred years ago, Pythagoras discovered something remarkable. By dividing a vibrating string in specific ratios — 2:1, 3:2, 4:3 — he could create harmonious musical intervals. An octave. A fifth. A fourth. But Pythagoras went further. He proposed that the same mathematical ratios governed the heavens. The planets, he said, were arranged according to harmonic intervals, creating a 'Music of the Spheres' — a cosmic symphony too sublime for human ears. For two thousand years, this idea persisted. Plato wrote that 'the stars perform the best of all songs.' Kepler, in his 1619 work Harmonices Mundi, calculated specific musical intervals for each planet's orbital motion. Newton acknowledged 'a certain most subtle spirit which pervades and lies hidden in all gross bodies' and described the 'supreme law of harmony in celestial bodies.'

Mathematical Foundations (1700s - 1800s) In the 18th and 19th centuries, mathematicians began to prove what Pythagoras had intuited. Sophie Germain developed wave equations showing that frequency creates form. Ernst Chladni demonstrated this visually: sprinkle sand on a vibrating plate, and it organizes into geometric patterns — cymatics. Different frequencies create different patterns. This was proof: frequency doesn't just correlate with form. Frequency CREATES form.

The Electrical Pioneers (1890s - 1940s) In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, a new wave of researchers applied these principles to electricity and biology. Nikola Tesla, perhaps the greatest inventor in history, understood the electromagnetic nature of reality more deeply than anyone of his era. 'If you want to find the secrets of the universe,' he said, 'think in terms of energy, frequency and vibration.' He also emphasized the significance of the numbers 3, 6, and 9 — numbers that, we'll see, underlie the frequency patterns of healing. Georges Lakhovsky, a Russian-French engineer, proposed in the 1920s that every living cell functions as an electromagnetic oscillator. Health, he argued, was 'oscillatory equilibrium' — cells vibrating at their optimal frequencies. Disease was 'oscillatory disequilibrium' — frequency disruption. Royal Raymond Rife took this further, claiming to have developed frequency devices that could destroy pathogens by matching their resonant frequencies. His work achieved remarkable results in clinical settings.
The Suppression (1910 - 1950) And then it stopped. The Flexner Report of 1910 restructured American medical education, defunding and discrediting electro-therapeutic approaches. The American

Medical Association, allied with pharmaceutical interests, systematically dismantled frequency-based medicine. Rife's equipment was confiscated. Lakhovsky died under mysterious circumstances in 1942. For decades, the frequency perspective was driven underground.

Modern Validation (1985 - Present) But truth has a way of resurfacing. In 1985, Dr. Robert O. Becker published 'The Body Electric,' documenting peer-reviewed research on bioelectricity and regeneration. He showed that the body is an electrical system, and that manipulating its currents could accelerate healing. In 1998, NASA's TRACE mission measured sound waves on the surface of the sun — confirming that stars literally vibrate, just as Pythagoras had proposed 2,500 years earlier. The HeartMath Institute has documented the heart's powerful electromagnetic field — 100 times stronger than the brain electrically, 5,000 times stronger magnetically. String Theory proposes that at the most fundamental level, particles are vibrating strings — frequency all the way down.

The Thread Was Never Broken What I've learned is that the frequency perspective was never wrong. It was suppressed, defunded, marginalized — but never disproven. The thread from Pythagoras to Tesla to Lakhovsky to modern bioelectromagnetics is continuous. We stand on the shoulders of 2,500 years of giants.
And now we have the tools — mathematical, computational, and experimental — to prove what they intuited.
E = hf The golden thread continues.

Galaxies as Electromagnetic Systems Galaxies aren't just gravitational structures. They're electromagnetic systems, threaded with magnetic fields averaging about 6 microgauss in spiral galaxies like our Milky Way. These magnetic fields follow the spiral arm structure. They're generated by the differential rotation of the galaxy — the inner regions spinning faster than the outer regions. This is a dynamo effect, converting rotational energy into magnetic field energy. And here's the key: this rotation has a frequency. The Sun takes about 230 million years to complete one orbit around the galactic center. That's a frequency of about 10⁻¹⁶ Hz. Extremely low — but real. And E = hf applies.

Density Waves The spiral arms of galaxies aren't static structures. They're density waves — regions of compression that rotate through the galactic disk, triggering star formation as they go. Lin and Shu demonstrated in 1964 that spiral structure emerges from a pattern frequency — the rate at which the density wave rotates. Stars pass through the wave, experiencing periodic compression. This is a frequency phenomenon at cosmic scale.

The Toroidal Field And here's something remarkable: the magnetic field of a galaxy forms a toroidal (donut) shape. The same geometry we'll see at every scale — in the solar system's heliosphere, in Earth's magnetosphere, in the heart's electromagnetic field, in the orbital shells of an electron. Planck's Revolution In 1900, Max Planck was trying to explain blackbody radiation. E = hf This single equation launched quantum mechanics and earned Planck the Nobel Prize. It's been confirmed by countless experiments. It's the foundation of modern physics.

Each element's electrons have specific allowed frequencies. E = hf determines atomic structure.
